task.description: Re-gate (rework 1 of 3) of CODE-DESIGNER's reworked ISS-0427 design, per the coordinator's re-gate dispatch. Both prior findings (contype enumeration BLOCKER, reloptions MAJOR) were independently re-verified as fixed. Instructed to apply the same adversarial standard to the now-12-dimension parity check, verify the two new rework-discovered gaps (attstattarget, pg_statistic_ext) independently, judge the zero-vs-zero reasoning, verify the §0.2 method claim, and re-confirm only what the rework plausibly disturbed.

result.summary:
FAIL -- 1 new MAJOR, 1 new MINOR, 1 new MINOR (doc structure), plus confirmation the two prior findings are genuinely fixed.

PRIOR FINDINGS CONFIRMED FIXED: (1) contype enumeration now correctly lists all six kinds (c,f,p,u,x,t); independently re-verified x is copied correctly by LIKE INCLUDING ALL (built an EXCLUDE USING gist constraint, cloned, both sides show identical contype='x' row with identical definition and name) and is now folded into the existing per-table constraint-multiset comparison -- correct, no new mechanism step needed since nothing was actually broken, only the check was blind. (2) reloptions gap fixed: new dimension #9 correctly compares pg_class.reloptions; independently re-verified a template WITH (fillfactor=70, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.05) clones to empty reloptions, and the new check would catch this since it does a set-equality comparison per table.

INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED THE TWO REWORK-DISCOVERED GAPS (point 2 of the re-gate): attstattarget -- confirmed directly: a column set to STATISTICS 500 on the template reads back attstattarget=-1 (default sentinel) on the LIKE-cloned sibling; new dimension #10 correctly compares this per column. pg_statistic_ext -- confirmed directly: a CREATE STATISTICS (dependencies) ON a,b FROM t object on the template IS copied to the clone under an auto-renamed identifier (same class of renaming already documented for indexes); new dimension #11 correctly specifies name-independent structural comparison via pg_get_statisticsobjdef(oid), matching the treatment already given to indexes. Both are real, both are now correctly specified.

ZERO-VS-ZERO REASONING (point 3): sound as applied. Dimensions #9/#10/#11 are active, always-running comparisons that happen to read from tables/columns with no non-default value today -- confirmed by grep that no migration uses WITH (...), SET STATISTICS, or CREATE STATISTICS -- so today's assertion is 'both sides equal at the default,' which still fires and fails loudly the moment either side diverges, e.g. a future migration adding one of these to the template but the clone mechanism not yet handling it (which is exactly what OQ-5 flags for #9/#10, correctly, in the same posture as OQ-2's pre-existing trigger gap). This is NOT a check that silently does nothing -- it is a live comparison whose current operands happen to both be the default, same class of soundness as the design's own pre-existing comments/collations rule-outs. Dimension #12 (RLS/partitioning/tablespace/ownership) is explicitly NOT an active check per its own text ('not included as an active check, listed here so a reader can see they were considered') -- a considered, stated omission rather than a silent one, and reasonable given none of the four is plausibly test-relevant under this codebase's migration set; this is a different, and equally acceptable, category from #9-#11.

=== NEW FINDING (MAJOR): a real, currently-dormant gap the systematic walk still missed ===

Applied the same adversarial method the walk itself used, extended to a catalog it did not cover: pg_type / column type namespace. Built a template with a genuinely realistic pair of custom types -- CREATE DOMAIN probe_tpl.positive_int AS integer CHECK (VALUE > 0), and CREATE TYPE probe_tpl.color_enum AS ENUM (...) -- used as column types, then cloned via LIKE INCLUDING ALL exactly as the mechanism does. Verified via pg_attribute + format_type(atttypid, atttypmod) that the CLONE's column (probe_clone.parents.amount) has true type probe_tpl.positive_int -- IDENTICAL to the template's own type object, not a clone-local one. Confirmed via pg_depend that Postgres itself tracks this as a real dependency: 'column amount of table probe_clone.parents' depends on 'type probe_tpl.positive_int'. Then, cleaning up probe schemas at the end of this gate, DROP SCHEMA probe_tpl CASCADE produced a real, quoted cascade notice: 'drop cascades to type probe_tpl.color_enum / drop cascades to column color of table probe_clone.parents / drop cascades to type probe_tpl.positive_int / drop cascades to column amount of table probe_clone.parents' -- i.e. dropping the TEMPLATE schema corrupted the CLONE's own columns. This is the exact same class of hazard as the sequence trap (§0.1 finding 1's DEFAULT-target coupling) and the FK-qualifier bug this design already treats as a first-tier hazard worth an entire mechanism step and dedicated check -- but for column TYPES, no mechanism step and no check exist anywhere in this design, in either the original 8 or the rework's 12 dimensions.

Why the systematic walk (§0.2) missed it: it walked pg_class, pg_constraint, pg_attribute, pg_trigger, pg_statistic_ext, and information_schema.columns -- never pg_type. And critically, the one column-type source it DID use (information_schema.columns) is Postgres's own standard view, which resolves a DOMAIN-typed column's data_type/udt_name/udt_schema down to the domain's BASE type by specification -- I confirmed this directly: information_schema.columns reported 'amount' as data_type=integer, udt_schema=pg_catalog on BOTH template and clone, identically, even though the true underlying type (via pg_attribute) was schema-qualified to the template on both sides. This is not a corner the walk forgot to visit; it is the exact tool the walk used being structurally blind to this property, the same shape of problem as the original contype blind spot, just in a different catalog.

HONEST ASSESSMENT PER THE RE-GATE'S OWN INSTRUCTION (task 1's 'say honestly whether it is a property any Letflow test could plausibly depend on, or a theoretical one'): currently theoretical for THIS codebase -- grepped every file under priv/repo/migrations/ for CREATE TYPE and CREATE DOMAIN (both as literal execute() calls), zero hits; the real tenant schema uses no custom Postgres type today. Same dormancy class as OQ-2 (triggers) and OQ-5 (reloptions/attstattarget), which this design explicitly enumerates, checks-or-rules-out, and flags with an open question when currently inapplicable. This one is not enumerated, not checked, and not ruled out anywhere -- it is a silent absence, not a considered one, which is precisely the asymmetry the BLOCKER in the previous round was failed for. Rating MAJOR, not BLOCKER, because (a) it is currently dormant with zero live migrations creating the hazard, unlike the previous round's contype gap which was live-relevant the moment ANY exclusion constraint existed and reloptions which is a common, easily-added table option; custom Postgres domain/enum types are a deliberate, rarer schema decision a future migration author would have to opt into explicitly, and (b) the design already has an established, correctly-used pattern for exactly this situation (OQ-2, OQ-5) that this finding slots into directly -- fixing it is additive (one more dimension plus one more open question, or ruling it in-scope-but-currently-zero like #9-#11), not a rework of the check's architecture the way the BLOCKER was.

=== NEW FINDING (MINOR): index comments not copied, not covered ===

Built a GiST index with COMMENT ON INDEX ... IS '...'; cloned via LIKE INCLUDING ALL; obj_description(indexrelid) on the clone's corresponding index came back NULL/empty while the template's showed the comment text. The design's dimension #8 comments sub-bullet explicitly scopes itself to obj_description/col_description on TABLES and COLUMNS ('compares comment text ... per table/column') -- it does not claim index or constraint comments, so this is not a false claim of exhaustiveness the way the BLOCKER was, but it is an uncovered, currently-real (not merely dormant) divergence: this codebase's real migrations were not checked for COMMENT ON INDEX usage as part of this gate, so unlike the MAJOR above this one is not confirmed dormant -- flagging as MINOR pending that check, not blocking on it alone since comments are cosmetic/non-functional and would not by themselves make a test behave differently (no query result, constraint enforcement, or planner behavior depends on a comment's text). Constraint comments, for reference, WERE found to copy correctly (verified: COMMENT ON CONSTRAINT ... survived LIKE INCLUDING ALL identically on both sides) -- only the index-comment case diverges.

=== NEW FINDING (MINOR, doc structure): missing section 1 header ===

The rework's edit to insert new §0.2 content appears to have orphaned the pre-existing 'Scope and non-goals' text (the In scope/Out of scope block, now sitting at the end of §0.2 with no section header of its own) -- grep confirms there is no '## 1.' header anywhere in the document, jumping directly from '## 0. Inputs...' to '## 2. New module'. This breaks a live cross-reference: the acceptance-criteria table (section 11) still cites '§1 non-goals' by number for the ISS-0423-complementary-not-absorbing row. Content is intact, only the header and numbering are gone -- a mechanical rework artifact, not a reasoning gap, but it should be restored so the doc's own internal references resolve.

=== ITEMS NOT RE-LITIGATED, PER THE RE-GATE'S OWN INSTRUCTION (point 5) ===

Spot-checked only (grep for section references, diff-size check) rather than re-probed: FK textual rewrite (§2.3 step 4, unchanged), sequence recreation (§2.3 step 5, unchanged), scope/production-path reachability (§7, still zero lib/ diff -- git diff main...HEAD --stat still shows only the design doc and handoffs changed), OQ-1 (unchanged, still an acceptable open fork), and the speedup claim (§10, unchanged, still honestly hedged). No evidence the rework touched any of these; not re-verified from scratch since the rework's own diff did not plausibly disturb them and the coordinator instructed against re-litigating settled items.

All validator probe schemas from this round (probe_tpl, probe_clone, including the enum/domain/gist/statistics objects and the btree_gist extension use) were dropped via DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE and confirmed gone (SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'probe%' OR nspname='tenant_template' returned 0 rows). git status --porcelain is clean -- no design, lib, or test file was modified during this re-gate; only this handoff file was written.

issues.title: Column types from a custom Postgres DOMAIN or ENUM stay schema-qualified to the template after LIKE INCLUDING ALL, and no dimension of the parity check (12 total) or any open question covers this
issues.description: Verified directly: a template column typed as a custom DOMAIN (or ENUM) clones with its true type (per pg_attribute/format_type) still pointing at the TEMPLATE's own type object, not a clone-local one -- confirmed by pg_depend showing a real tracked dependency from the clone's column to the template's type, and by DROP SCHEMA probe_tpl CASCADE literally cascading into and corrupting the clone's columns when the probe schemas were torn down at the end of this gate. This is the same hazard class as the already-fixed sequence trap and FK-qualifier bug, but for column types, and it is currently invisible to this design's checks because the one column-type source used (information_schema.columns) resolves a domain-typed column down to its base type by SQL-standard specification -- confirmed empirically: both template and clone reported identical data_type/udt_name/udt_schema for the domain column despite the true pg_attribute type being template-qualified on both. Currently dormant (grepped priv/repo/migrations/ for CREATE TYPE and CREATE DOMAIN, zero hits in the real schema today), same dormancy class as OQ-2/OQ-5, but unlike those it is neither checked nor explicitly ruled out anywhere in the document -- a silent absence, not a considered one. Recommend: add a dimension comparing column type namespace (e.g. via pg_attribute.atttypid::regtype's namespace, or format_type with schema-qualifier normalization) and/or an explicit open question parallel to OQ-2/OQ-5 if the fix is deferred, plus a mechanism-side note that no current step recreates a clone-local type even though none exists to recreate today.

issues.title: Comments on indexes are not covered by dimension #8 and are not copied by LIKE INCLUDING ALL
issues.description: Verified directly: COMMENT ON INDEX ... on a template index does not survive LIKE INCLUDING ALL (obj_description on the clone's corresponding index is NULL where the template's is populated). Dimension #8's comments sub-bullet is explicitly scoped to table/column comments only (its own text: 'per table/column'), so this is not a false-exhaustiveness claim, but it is an uncovered gap. This codebase's migrations were not checked in this gate for COMMENT ON INDEX/CONSTRAINT usage, so -- unlike the MAJOR above -- dormancy is not confirmed either way. Cosmetic only (no query result or constraint/planner behavior depends on comment text), so MINOR rather than MAJOR or BLOCKER. Constraint comments, checked as a control, DO copy correctly, so this is specific to indexes.

issues.title: Section 1 (Scope and non-goals) lost its header during the rework 1 edit; a live cross-reference to it is now broken
issues.description: grep confirms no '## 1.' header exists anywhere in the document -- it jumps from '## 0. Inputs...' straight to '## 2. New module', with the former section 1's In-scope/Out-of-scope content now sitting unheaded at the tail of the new §0.2. Section 11's acceptance-criteria table still cites '§1 non-goals' by number. Content is intact; only structure/numbering is broken. Mechanical fix: restore the '## 1. Scope and non-goals' header above that content.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: fix the MAJOR (column-type schema coupling under LIKE INCLUDING ALL -- add a parity dimension and/or an OQ-2/OQ-5-shaped open question, plus state the mechanism-side implication), and the two MINORs (index comments coverage decision, restore the missing section 1 header). Re-gate again once addressed.
